result.abstract: The lecture describes the 22 bones of the skull: the 8 cranial bones of the neurocranium and the 14 facial bones of the viscerocranium, and how the skull sits on the neck. It goes bone by bone through the sphenoid, ethmoid, temporal, zygomatic, maxilla, small nasal bones and mandible, with their parts, foramina and what passes through them. It ends with the base of the skull and its three cranial fossae, and the four paired paranasal sinuses and their drainage.

concepts.name: Skull
concepts.definition: The bony framework of the head, made of 22 bones: 8 cranial bones that wrap the brain and 14 facial bones. It rests on the atlas (C1).

evidence.quote: The skull has 22 bones
22 skull bones = 8 cranial + 14 facial

concepts.name: Neurocranium
concepts.definition: The eight skull bones that enclose and protect the brain: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, two parietal and two temporal. It is divided into the calvaria and the base.

evidence.quote: Eight of them wrap the brain (the neurocranium)
consist of eight bones

concepts.name: Viscerocranium
concepts.definition: The 14 facial bones that shape the face, jaws, nose and eye sockets: six paired bones (maxilla, zygomatic, palatine, nasal, lacrimal, inferior nasal concha) and the unpaired mandible and vomer.

evidence.quote: fourteen shape the face, jaws, nose and eye sockets (the viscerocranium)
These bones are collectively known as the viscerocranium and provide

concepts.name: Calvaria
concepts.definition: The skull cap: the roof part of the neurocranium, as opposed to the base. The slides list its bones as the frontal, occipital and two parietal bones.

evidence.quote: The neurocranium is split into the calvaria (the skull cap) and the base
Calvarium bones: frontal, occipital and two parietal bones

concepts.name: Base of the skull
concepts.definition: The floor of the cranial cavity, made of five bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, temporal and occipital. Seen from inside it forms three steps, the anterior, middle and posterior cranial fossae.

evidence.quote: The floor of the cranial cavity is made of five bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, temporal and occipital
Skull base bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, temporal, occipital

concepts.name: Atlanto-occipital joint
concepts.definition: The joint where the skull rests on the atlas (C1). It allows nodding, the 'yes' movement.

evidence.quote: The atlanto-occipital joint allows nodding
Atlanto-occipital joint = nodding

concepts.name: Atlanto-axial joint
concepts.definition: The joint where the atlas turns on the axis (C2). It allows rotation, the 'no' movement.

evidence.quote: The atlanto-axial joint allows rotation
Atlanto-axial joint = rotation

concepts.name: Frontal bone
concepts.definition: Single cranial bone that forms the forehead and the roof of the orbits.

evidence.quote: It forms the forehead and the roof of the orbits, and is one of the 8 cranial bones
Forehead; forms the roof of the orbit

concepts.name: Parietal bone
concepts.definition: Paired cranial bone forming the sides and roof of the skull.

evidence.quote: There are two, and they form the sides and roof of the skull
Sides and roof of the skull

concepts.name: Temporal bone
concepts.definition: Paired cranial bone at the sides and base of the skull that holds the ear structures. Its parts are squamous, petrous, tympanic and mastoid, plus the styloid process.

evidence.quote: Sides and base; holds the ear structures
Squamous, petrous, tympanic and mastoid parts, plus the styloid process

concepts.name: Occipital bone
concepts.definition: Single cranial bone at the back and base of the skull; the foramen magnum is in it.

evidence.quote: Back and base; the foramen magnum is here

concepts.name: Sphenoid bone
concepts.definition: Single central bone of the skull base, with a body, two greater wings, two lesser wings and two pterygoid processes.

evidence.quote: Central bone of the skull base
Body, two greater wings, two lesser wings, two pterygoid processes

concepts.name: Ethmoid bone
concepts.definition: Single cranial bone between the eye sockets that forms the roof of the nasal cavity. Its four parts are the cribriform plate, crista galli, perpendicular plate and the two ethmoidal labyrinths.

evidence.quote: Between the eye sockets; roof of the nasal cavity
Cribriform plate, crista galli, perpendicular plate, and the two ethmoidal labyrinths

concepts.name: Sella turcica
concepts.definition: A saddle-shaped depression on the upper surface of the body of the sphenoid. It holds the pituitary gland in the hypophysial fossa, with the tuberculum sellae in front and the dorsum sellae behind.

evidence.quote: A saddle-shaped depression on the upper surface of the sphenoid body
pituitary gland on body on top

concepts.name: Greater wing of the sphenoid
concepts.definition: Part of the sphenoid forming the floor of the middle cranial fossa, part of the lateral skull wall and the back of the lateral orbital wall. It has the foramen rotundum, foramen ovale and foramen spinosum.

evidence.quote: Form the floor of the middle cranial fossa, part of the lateral skull wall and the back of the lateral orbital wall
foramen rotundum (V2), ovale (V3) and spinosum (middle meningeal vessels) in the greater wing

concepts.name: Lesser wing of the sphenoid
concepts.definition: Part of the sphenoid that separates the anterior and middle cranial fossae, forms the lateral border of the optic canal and carries the anterior clinoid process.

evidence.quote: Separate the anterior and middle cranial fossae. Form the lateral border of the optic canal

concepts.name: Pterygoid process
concepts.definition: Paired process of the sphenoid that hangs down from where the body meets the greater wing. Each has a medial and a lateral plate, for muscle attachment.

evidence.quote: Hang down from where the body meets the greater wing. Each has a medial and a lateral plate, for muscle attachment
pterygoid = pterygoid muscles to allow chewing = paired

concepts.name: Foramen rotundum
concepts.definition: Opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid, in the middle cranial fossa, that transmits the maxillary nerve (V2).

evidence.quote: Foramen rotundum: maxillary nerve (V2)
Foramen rotundum carries V2, foramen ovale carries V3 (mandibular nerve)

concepts.name: Foramen ovale
concepts.definition: Opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid, in the middle cranial fossa, that transmits the mandibular nerve (V3).

evidence.quote: Foramen ovale: mandibular nerve (V3)

concepts.name: Foramen spinosum
concepts.definition: Opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid, in the middle cranial fossa, that transmits the middle meningeal vessels.

evidence.quote: Foramen spinosum: middle meningeal vessels
Foramen spinosum = middle meningeal artery

concepts.name: Optic canal
concepts.definition: Opening of the middle cranial fossa whose lateral border is formed by the lesser wing of the sphenoid and whose medial border is formed by the body of the sphenoid.

evidence.quote: The lesser wing forms the lateral border of the optic canal (the body forms the medial border)

concepts.name: Superior orbital fissure
concepts.definition: The gap between the lesser and greater wings of the sphenoid, one of the openings of the middle cranial fossa. The lecture's mnemonic assigns it V1.

evidence.quote: The superior orbital fissure is the gap between the lesser and greater wings
The superior orbital fissure lies between the lesser and greater wings

concepts.name: Maxillary nerve
concepts.definition: The V2 nerve of the trigeminal, which passes through the foramen rotundum in the greater wing of the sphenoid. Its palatine branches run through the greater and lesser palatine foramina.

evidence.quote: Foramen rotundum: maxillary nerve (V2)
Greater and lesser palatine foramina carry palatine branches of V2

concepts.name: Mandibular nerve
concepts.definition: The V3 nerve of the trigeminal, which passes through the foramen ovale in the greater wing of the sphenoid. The inferior alveolar nerve comes from it.

evidence.quote: foramen ovale carries V3 (mandibular nerve)

concepts.name: Middle meningeal artery
concepts.definition: Vessel that passes through the foramen spinosum. Its anterior branch lies under the pterion.

evidence.quote: Foramen spinosum = middle meningeal artery
over the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery

concepts.name: Cribriform plate
concepts.definition: Sieve-like shelf of the ethmoid that forms the roof of the nasal cavity and part of the anterior cranial fossa. Its foramina carry the olfactory nerve fibres (CN I) up to the brain.

evidence.quote: Sieve-like shelf that forms the roof of the nasal cavity
ethmoid through cribriform plate to reach brain

concepts.name: Crista galli
concepts.definition: Upward projection of the midline plate of the ethmoid; it anchors the falx cerebri.

evidence.quote: Upward projection of the midline plate; anchors the falx cerebri

concepts.name: Perpendicular plate of the ethmoid
concepts.definition: Plate of the ethmoid that hangs down from the cribriform plate and forms the upper part of the bony nasal septum.

evidence.quote: Hangs down from the cribriform plate; forms the upper part of the bony nasal septum

concepts.name: Ethmoidal labyrinth
concepts.definition: Paired part of the ethmoid that holds the ethmoidal air cells. Each has a paper-thin orbital plate (lamina papyracea) on the eye-socket side and a medial sheet from which the superior and middle nasal conchae project.

evidence.quote: Hold the ethmoidal air cells. Each has a paper-thin orbital plate (lamina papyracea) on the eye-socket side
The ethmoidal air cells, the lamina papyracea (orbital plate), and the superior and middle nasal conchae

concepts.name: Olfactory nerve
concepts.definition: Cranial nerve I, whose fibres pass from the nasal cavity through the foramina of the cribriform plate up to the brain, for the olfactory sense.

evidence.quote: Its foramina carry the olfactory nerve fibres (CN I) up to the brain
from the nose, nerve reach brain for olfactory

concepts.name: Squamous part of the temporal bone
concepts.definition: Large flat plate of the temporal bone on the side of the skull. It gives origin to temporalis, carries the zygomatic process and has the mandibular fossa below it.

evidence.quote: Large flat plate on the side of the skull. Origin of temporalis

concepts.name: Petrous part of the temporal bone
concepts.definition: Dense, pyramid-shaped part of the temporal bone that separates the middle and posterior cranial fossae and protects the inner ear. It has the internal acoustic meatus, carotid canal and jugular foramen.

evidence.quote: Dense, pyramid-shaped part that separates the middle and posterior cranial fossae and protects the inner ear

concepts.name: Tympanic part of the temporal bone
concepts.definition: Curved plate of the temporal bone that forms much of the external acoustic meatus.

evidence.quote: Curved plate that forms much of the external acoustic meatus

concepts.name: Mastoid part of the temporal bone
concepts.definition: Part of the temporal bone that contains the mastoid air cells. Its mastoid process is an attachment for sternocleidomastoid.

evidence.quote: Contains the mastoid air cells. The mastoid process is an attachment for sternocleidomastoid

concepts.name: Mandibular fossa
concepts.definition: Hollow on the underside of the squamous part of the temporal bone, behind the articular eminence. It receives the head (condyle) of the mandible at the temporomandibular joint.

evidence.quote: Hollow on the underside of the squamous part, behind the articular eminence
It is on the squamous part of the temporal bone and receives the head of the mandible

concepts.name: Styloid process
concepts.definition: Thin spike of the temporal bone pointing down and forward, giving attachment to stylopharyngeus, styloglossus and stylohyoid. The stylomastoid foramen just behind it carries the facial nerve.

evidence.quote: Thin spike pointing down and forward
Styloid process (gives attachment to muscle and ligaments)

concepts.name: Zygomatic process of the temporal bone
concepts.definition: Process of the squamous part of the temporal bone that meets the zygomatic bone to form the zygomatic arch.

evidence.quote: Its zygomatic process meets the zygomatic bone to form the zygomatic arch
Zygomatic part process (form the zygomatic arch with the temporal process of the

concepts.name: Zygomatic arch
concepts.definition: Bony arch formed by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone joining the temporal process of the zygomatic bone at the temporozygomatic suture.

evidence.quote: The arch is completed by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone joining the temporal process of the zygomatic bone at the temporozygomatic suture

concepts.name: Temporomandibular joint
concepts.definition: The joint where the head of the mandible articulates with the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone. The mandible moves here.

evidence.quote: the head articulates with the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone (temporomandibular joint)
Connects with the cranium base at the

concepts.name: Pterion
concepts.definition: H-shaped meeting point on the side of the skull of four bones: frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and greater wing of the sphenoid. It is the thinnest part of the skull wall and lies over the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery.

evidence.quote: The pterion is the H-shaped meeting point on the side of the skull of four bones
thinnest part of the skull, over the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery

concepts.name: Extradural haematoma
concepts.definition: Condition that the lecture links to a blow to the temple at the pterion, where the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery can be torn; it is noted with a lucid interval.

evidence.quote: blow to the temple → extradural haematoma (lucid interval)

concepts.name: Zygomatic bone
concepts.definition: The cheekbone: a diamond-shaped paired facial bone forming the prominence of the cheek, part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit, and part of the zygomatic arch. It has frontal, temporal and maxillary processes.

evidence.quote: it forms the prominence of the cheek, part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit, and part of the zygomatic arch
three processes (frontal, temporal, maxillary)

concepts.name: Maxilla
concepts.definition: The upper jaw: a paired facial bone with a pyramid-shaped body containing the maxillary sinus and four processes (frontal, zygomatic, alveolar, palatine). The two maxillae form the middle third of the face.

evidence.quote: The two maxillae fuse at the midline and form the middle third of the face
A pyramid-shaped body containing the maxillary sinus, plus four processes: frontal, zygomatic, alveolar and palatine

concepts.name: Maxillary sinus
concepts.definition: The largest paranasal sinus, in the body of the maxilla. It opens into the middle meatus at the hiatus semilunaris; its ostium is high on its medial wall and its floor lies near the upper molar roots.

evidence.quote: The maxillary sinus lies in the body of the maxilla and is the largest
The maxillary sinus ostium is high on its medial wall

concepts.name: Frontal process of the maxilla
concepts.definition: Process of the maxilla that runs up between the nasal and lacrimal bones and contributes to the lacrimal fossa.

evidence.quote: Runs up between the nasal and lacrimal bones; contributes to the lacrimal fossa

concepts.name: Zygomatic process of the maxilla
concepts.definition: Process of the maxilla that meets the zygomatic bone.

evidence.quote: Meets the zygomatic bone

concepts.name: Alveolar process of the maxilla
concepts.definition: Process of the maxilla that holds the upper teeth, with 8 sockets on each side.

evidence.quote: Holds the upper teeth (8 sockets on each side)

concepts.name: Palatine process of the maxilla
concepts.definition: Horizontal shelf of the maxilla forming the front part of the hard palate and the nasal floor.

evidence.quote: Horizontal shelf forming the front part of the hard palate and the nasal floor

concepts.name: Infraorbital foramen
concepts.definition: Opening in the maxilla just below the inferior orbital margin, where the infraorbital nerve and vessels emerge onto the face after the infraorbital groove and canal.

evidence.quote: The infraorbital foramen, in the maxilla just below the inferior orbital margin
the infraorbital nerve and vessels emerge here after the infraorbital groove and canal

concepts.name: Nasal bone
concepts.definition: Paired slender facial bone forming the bridge of the nose; the two meet at the internasal suture.

evidence.quote: Slender bones forming the bridge of the nose; meet at the internasal suture
two slender bones at the bridge of the nose

concepts.name: Vomer
concepts.definition: Unpaired, plough-shaped facial bone that forms the lower and posterior part of the bony nasal septum; it meets the palatine, maxilla and ethmoid.

evidence.quote: Forms the lower and posterior part of the bony nasal septum; meets the palatine, maxilla and ethmoid
Makes the posterior slant of the nasal septum

concepts.name: Palatine bone
concepts.definition: Paired L-shaped facial bone with a horizontal plate (posterior hard palate and nasal floor) and a perpendicular plate (lateral nasal wall). It also adds a small part of the orbital floor.

evidence.quote: L-shaped, with a horizontal plate (posterior part of the hard palate and nasal floor) and a perpendicular plate (lateral nasal wall)
Located at the back of the oral cavity

concepts.name: Horizontal plate of the palatine bone
concepts.definition: Plate of the palatine bone that forms the posterior part of the hard palate and the nasal floor.

evidence.quote: horizontal plate (posterior hard palate and nasal floor)
the horizontal plates of the palatine bones complete it behind

concepts.name: Inferior nasal concha
concepts.definition: Paired separate facial bone on the lateral nasal wall that supports the inferior turbinate. The superior and middle conchae, by contrast, belong to the ethmoid.

evidence.quote: Separate bone on the lateral nasal wall; supports the inferior turbinate
The inferior nasal concha is a separate bone

concepts.name: Lacrimal bone
concepts.definition: Paired small facial bone on the medial wall of the orbit; it helps form the lacrimal fossa and the nasolacrimal groove.

evidence.quote: Small bone on the medial wall of the orbit; helps form the lacrimal fossa and the nasolacrimal groove
The tiniest bones of the face

concepts.name: Mandible
concepts.definition: The lower jaw, an unpaired facial bone and the only bone of the skull that moves. It has a horseshoe-shaped body and two rami that meet the body at the angle.

evidence.quote: It has a horseshoe-shaped body and two rami that meet the body at the angle
Mandible, the lower jaw, and the only skull bone that moves

concepts.name: Body of the mandible
concepts.definition: Curved, horseshoe-shaped part of the mandible whose upper alveolar part holds the lower teeth. Its two halves fuse at the midline (symphysis).

evidence.quote: Curved; the upper alveolar part holds the lower teeth. The two halves fuse at the midline (symphysis)

concepts.name: Ramus of the mandible
concepts.definition: Vertical part of the mandible. Its upper border has the coronoid process in front, the condylar process behind, and the mandibular notch between them.

evidence.quote: Its upper border has the coronoid process in front, the condylar process behind, and the mandibular notch between them

concepts.name: Mental foramen
concepts.definition: Opening on the outer surface of the body of the mandible, below the premolars. It transmits the mental nerve and vessels.

evidence.quote: The mental foramen, on the outer surface of the body of the mandible. It transmits the mental nerve and vessels
On the outer surface of the body, below the premolars

concepts.name: Mandibular foramen
concepts.definition: Opening on the inner surface of the ramus of the mandible, where the inferior alveolar nerve and vessels enter to run in the mandibular canal.

evidence.quote: On the inner surface of the ramus. The inferior alveolar nerve and vessels enter here and run in the mandibular canal

concepts.name: Coronoid process
concepts.definition: Triangular, flattened process at the front of the upper border of the ramus of the mandible; the temporalis muscle inserts here.

evidence.quote: Triangular, flattened; the temporalis muscle inserts here

concepts.name: Condylar process
concepts.definition: Process at the back of the upper border of the ramus of the mandible, with a head and neck. The head articulates with the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint.

evidence.quote: Head and neck; the head articulates with the mandibular fossa of the temporal bone

concepts.name: Mandibular notch
concepts.definition: The deep concavity on the upper border of the ramus of the mandible, between the coronoid process in front and the condylar process behind.

evidence.quote: The mandibular notch is the deep concavity between the coronoid process in front and the condylar process behind

concepts.name: Sublingual fossa
concepts.definition: Fossa on the inner surface of the body of the mandible, above the mylohyoid line and near the midline. It lodges the sublingual gland.

evidence.quote: Inner surface of the body, above the mylohyoid line and near the midline. Lodges the sublingual gland

concepts.name: Submandibular fossa
concepts.definition: Fossa on the inner surface of the body of the mandible, below the mylohyoid line. It lodges the submandibular gland.

evidence.quote: Inner surface of the body, below the mylohyoid line. Lodges the submandibular gland

concepts.name: Mental protuberance
concepts.definition: The chin: the triangular prominence in the midline of the outer surface of the mandible.

evidence.quote: The chin: the triangular prominence in the midline of the outer surface

concepts.name: Inferior alveolar nerve
concepts.definition: Nerve from V3 that enters the mandibular foramen and runs forward through the mandibular canal, supplying sensation to the lower teeth. Near the front it divides into the mental nerve and the incisive nerve.

evidence.quote: The inferior alveolar nerve enters the mandibular foramen and runs forward through the mandibular canal, supplying sensation to the lower teeth
The inferior alveolar nerve (from V3) enters the mandibular foramen and runs in the mandibular canal

concepts.name: Mental nerve
concepts.definition: Terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve that leaves the mandible through the mental foramen.

evidence.quote: the mental nerve, which leaves through the mental foramen

concepts.name: Mandibular canal
concepts.definition: Canal of the mandible in which the inferior alveolar nerve and vessels run forward after entering at the mandibular foramen.

evidence.quote: enters the mandibular foramen and runs forward through the mandibular canal

concepts.name: Temporalis muscle
concepts.definition: Muscle that takes origin from the squamous part of the temporal bone and inserts on the coronoid process of the mandible.

evidence.quote: the temporalis muscle inserts here
Large flat plate on the side of the skull. Origin of temporalis

concepts.name: Bony nasal septum
concepts.definition: The bony partition of the nose, formed by the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid (upper part) and the vomer (lower and posterior part), with septal cartilage in front.

evidence.quote: The perpendicular plate of the ethmoid (upper part) and the vomer (lower and posterior part), with septal cartilage in front
Nasal septum: perpendicular plate of the ethmoid + vomer

concepts.name: Hard palate
concepts.definition: The bony palate, made by the palatine processes of the maxillae in front and the horizontal plates of the palatine bones behind.

evidence.quote: The hard palate is made by the palatine processes of the maxillae in front and the horizontal plates of the palatine bones behind

concepts.name: Anterior cranial fossa
concepts.definition: The front step of the floor of the cranial cavity, holding the frontal lobes. It is formed by the orbital plates of the frontal, the cribriform plate of the ethmoid and the lesser wings of the sphenoid; its openings are the cribriform foramina.

evidence.quote: The anterior fossa (frontal lobes) is formed by the frontal, ethmoid and sphenoid
Orbital plates of the frontal, cribriform plate of the ethmoid, lesser wings of the sphenoid

concepts.name: Middle cranial fossa
concepts.definition: The middle step of the floor of the cranial cavity, holding the temporal lobes and formed by the sphenoid and temporal bones. Its openings include the optic canal, superior orbital fissure, foramen rotundum, ovale, spinosum and lacerum, and the carotid canal.

evidence.quote: The middle fossa (temporal lobes) is formed by the sphenoid and temporal bones
middle (optic canal, SOF, rotundum, ovale, spinosum, lacerum, carotid canal)

concepts.name: Posterior cranial fossa
concepts.definition: The back step of the floor of the cranial cavity, holding the cerebellum and formed by the temporal and occipital bones. Its openings are the internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal and foramen magnum.

evidence.quote: The posterior fossa (cerebellum) is formed by the temporal and occipital bones and holds the foramen magnum
posterior (internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal, foramen magnum)

concepts.name: Foramen magnum
concepts.definition: Opening in the occipital bone, in the posterior cranial fossa. From below it is seen with the occipital condyles.

evidence.quote: Back and base; the foramen magnum is here

concepts.name: Paranasal sinus
concepts.definition: One of four pairs of air-filled spaces around the nasal cavity, named after the bones that hold them: frontal, ethmoidal, sphenoid and maxillary. They drain into the nasal cavity.

evidence.quote: Four pairs of air-filled spaces around the nasal cavity, named after the bones that hold them
Frontal sinus, maxillary sinuses, ethmoid sinuses, sphenoidal sinuses

concepts.name: Frontal sinus
concepts.definition: Paranasal sinus in the frontal bone, behind the eyebrows. It drains into the middle meatus through the frontonasal duct and infundibulum.

evidence.quote: Frontal bone, behind the eyebrows
Middle meatus, through the frontonasal duct and infundibulum

concepts.name: Ethmoidal sinus
concepts.definition: Paranasal sinus made of the air cells in the ethmoidal labyrinths. The anterior cells drain into the middle meatus and the posterior cells into the superior meatus.

evidence.quote: Air cells in the ethmoidal labyrinths
Anterior cells: middle meatus. Posterior cells: superior meatus

concepts.name: Sphenoid sinus
concepts.definition: Paranasal sinus in the body of the sphenoid. It drains into the sphenoethmoidal recess.

evidence.quote: Central, cube-like. Contains the sphenoid sinuses
Sphenoid: the sphenoethmoidal recess above the superior concha

concepts.name: Middle meatus
concepts.definition: Part of the nasal cavity that receives the frontal, anterior ethmoid and maxillary sinuses, all close together near the hiatus semilunaris.

evidence.quote: The middle meatus receives the frontal, anterior ethmoid and maxillary sinuses, all close together near the hiatus semilunaris

concepts.name: Superior meatus
concepts.definition: Part of the nasal cavity into which the posterior ethmoidal cells drain.

evidence.quote: Superior meatus: posterior ethmoid cells

concepts.name: Sphenoethmoidal recess
concepts.definition: Recess of the nasal cavity above the superior concha, into which the sphenoid sinus drains.

evidence.quote: Sphenoid: the sphenoethmoidal recess above the superior concha

concepts.name: Orbit
concepts.definition: The eye socket, a cavity built by 7 bones: frontal, sphenoid, ethmoid, zygomatic, lacrimal, maxilla and palatine.

evidence.quote: The orbit, built by 7 bones: frontal, sphenoid, ethmoid, zygomatic, lacrimal, maxilla and palatine

concepts.name: Supraorbital notch
concepts.definition: Notch (or foramen) in the superior orbital margin of the frontal bone. It transmits the supraorbital nerve and vessels.

evidence.quote: The supraorbital notch (or foramen), in the superior orbital margin of the frontal bone

concepts.name: Piriform aperture
concepts.definition: The bony opening of the nasal cavity, bounded by the nasal bones and the maxillae.

evidence.quote: The piriform aperture, the bony opening of the nasal cavity, bounded by the nasal bones and the maxillae

relations.statement: Eight of the 22 skull bones wrap the brain and make up the neurocranium.

evidence.quote: The skull has 22 bones. Eight of them wrap the brain (the neurocranium)

relations.statement: Fourteen of the 22 skull bones are facial bones and make up the viscerocranium.

evidence.quote: 22 bones: the neurocranium (8 bones, protects the brain) and the viscerocranium (14 facial bones, including the mandible)

relations.statement: The neurocranium is split into the calvaria (skull cap) and the base.

evidence.quote: The neurocranium is split into the calvaria (the skull cap) and the base

relations.statement: The neurocranium is split into the calvaria and the base, the floor of the cranial cavity.

evidence.quote: The neurocranium is split into the calvaria (the skull cap) and the base. The base is the floor of the cranial cavity

relations.statement: The atlanto-occipital joint joins the skull to the atlas and allows nodding.

evidence.quote: Atlanto-occipital joint (skull on the atlas): nodding

relations.statement: The atlanto-occipital joint gives nodding ('yes'), the atlanto-axial joint gives rotation ('no').

evidence.quote: Atlanto-occipital joint = nodding. Atlanto-axial joint = rotation

relations.statement: The frontal bone is one of the 8 cranial bones.

evidence.quote: Frontal bone. It forms the forehead and the roof of the orbits, and is one of the 8 cranial bones

evidence.quote: Cranial bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietal, 2 temporal

relations.statement: The two temporal bones are cranial bones.

evidence.quote: Cranial bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietal, 2 temporal

relations.statement: The occipital bone is a cranial bone.

evidence.quote: Cranial bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietal, 2 temporal

relations.statement: The sphenoid is a cranial bone.

evidence.quote: Cranial bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietal, 2 temporal

relations.statement: The ethmoid is a cranial bone, not a facial bone.

evidence.quote: Cranial bones: frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, occipital, 2 parietal, 2 temporal
